correctness.rationale: Rank-one commutation with nilpotent \(N\) forces \(NT=TN=0\); square-zero is the scalar pairing \(\varphi(u)=0\). The pairing has rank equal to the number of size-one blocks, giving the total count. Rank-one update conditions and a predecessor map of rank equal to the number of length-two blocks give \(C_+,C_-\). Powers of \(N+T\) coincide with powers of \(N\) from exponent two, forcing the exact Jordan change. Incidence hyperplane rank determines geometric components. Direct verification exhaustively checked 90 tensor-parameter cases over fields 2,3,4,5 and eight full ambient matrix spaces; neither finite test is substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: The problem asks for the complete Jordan type distribution of the most elementary nontrivial nilpotent perturbation constrained by a fixed centralizer, a natural structural stratum in commuting nilpotent matrix geometry. The new rank-refined counts yield three sharp transition cases for every partition beyond the previously known unweighted fiber total, and a geometric reducibility criterion detecting exactly one size-one block. The count for partitions \((4,2,1)\) and \((3,3,1)\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) is identically 176 but 9 versus 0 rank-decreasing transitions, proving the refinement detects length-two information absent from the unweighted census. The main claim is not merely a small numerical improvement.
